name: Risk or Safety: exact optimal-play win probabilities beyond n = 30 (OEIS A387261/A387262)
compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (exact policy iteration over O(n^3) positions with big rationals, one strongly connected component at a time; measure growth at n >= 31)
statement: Two players race to n banked points. On a turn the player tosses a fair coin: each head adds one open point and the player may then stop, banking the open points (turn passes), or toss again; a tail loses all open points and passes the turn. First to n points wins; equivalently each turn chooses a number x of coins and banks x points iff all are heads. Jehn ('Optimal strategy in the game Risk or Safety', arXiv:2603.01002, March 2026) proves the solution is unique (following Glenn-Fang-Kruskal's argument for Can't Stop), solves n <= 6 analytically (first-player win probability 6/11 for n = 3, 2236/4165 for n = 4, 1026/1925 for n = 5, 275848876/521145625 for n = 6) and finds optimal strategies up to n = 20 by an interval iteration (paper Table 1; OEIS A394776, b-file of 400 terms). Exact optimal-play win probabilities of the starting player are published only for n = 1..15, in OEIS A387261 (numerators) and A387262 (denominators), both keyword 'hard'; e.g. n = 15: 14364898791782224577113184680141626682/27711032758513212360715995025634765625. A387260 counts strategies (8 terms). The rules appear to coincide with the coin variant of the dice game Pig ('Piglet') analysed by Neller and Presser; that source was not read for this entry, so check it for prior exact values before claiming novelty. The original proposal reported OEIS terms only through n = 15 on 2026-10-14; the earlier page review could not retrieve the OEIS entries. Terms n = 16..30 were subsequently merged in V3R1T4S PR #169. The open extension starts at n = 31; no new OEIS frontier check was made here. The earlier page review could not retrieve the OEIS sources (HTTP 403); the merged repository terms are recorded separately below.
success_criterion: Exact reduced rationals A387261(n)/A387262(n) - the starting player's win probability from (0 open, 0 banked, 0 banked) under optimal play by both players - for EVERY n from 31 through 45 (direction: new terms), each with a certificate: the claimed value P(a, b, c) for every position (a open and b banked points of the player to move, c banked by the opponent) and the claimed action, satisfying exactly P(a, b, c) = max(continue, stop) for a >= 1 and the forced toss for a = 0, where continue = (1/2)(1 - P(0, c, b)) + (1/2) P(a + 1, b, c) and stop = 1 - P(0, c, a + b), with P = 1 when a + b >= n (equations of Sections 3-4 of arXiv:2603.01002), all checked in exact arithmetic. The same code must reproduce the published or merged terms for n <= 30 (or certify a correction, see p1). Check the OEIS entries, b-files, edit histories and merged repository results before claiming; terms already established there do not count as new terms.

partial_wins.statement: A certified correction: an exact Bellman certificate showing that a published value (A387261/A387262, n <= 30, including the merged terms in PR #169) or a published optimal action (paper Table 1 / A394776, n <= 20) is not optimal.

Certified exact terms for every n = 31..35 with complete independently checked Bellman value/action tables, after calibration on published and merged terms through n = 30. Already merged terms n = 16..30 do not count.

verification_method: A short checker in Python fractions reads the claimed value and action tables, checks terminal positions, then checks at every non-terminal position that the claimed value equals the maximum of the two action values computed from the table itself (only the toss at a = 0) and that the claimed action attains it. Every strategy pair ends the game with probability 1 (banked totals never fall and each turn has positive probability of progress), so these equations have a unique solution (Jehn Section 2) and the check proves optimality. Reduce P(0,0,0) and compare with OEIS; calibrate on the closed forms for n <= 6 and the published and merged terms for n <= 30, including PR #169.
status_checked: 2026-10-14; historical proposal date preserved. No fresh source request was made during final preparation. The earlier page review could not retrieve the OEIS sources (HTTP 403); the merged repository terms are recorded separately below. Terms n = 16..30 were merged in V3R1T4S PR #169. The open extension range starts at n = 31. This supplied repository-status update does not claim that OEIS has incorporated the terms.
angles: Banked scores never decrease, so positions split into components with a fixed pair {b, c}; solve components in decreasing b + c, each a small two-player stochastic game, by exact policy iteration.
Find the policy in floating point first, then do one exact rational solve per component and an exact policy-improvement check.
Numerators reach 38 digits at n = 15 and keep growing: use GMP or FLINT rationals.
Cross-check the action table against A394776's encoding (n = (j-1)^2 + i if i < j, else i^2 - j + 1, for i points needed by the mover and j by the opponent).
pitfalls: At a = 0 the player must toss; stopping with no open points is not an action.
Reaching n with open points counts as a win (the paper sets P = 1 when a + b = n).
Near-ties can flip a floating-point policy choice; decide actions only after an exact comparison.
OEIS 'hard' reflects the original method, not the problem; the main risk is a rules mismatch (who moves first, banking at n), so reproduce n <= 6 exactly before scaling up.
If the game is exactly Neller-Presser's Piglet, earlier exact or numerical work may exist for some n; check before claiming.
